data.title: 'Death of the Soccer God' pays 'homage' to Haitian diaspora and 'those who go back & do their best'
data.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Dimitry Elias Léger, journalist and author of "Death of the Soccer God". He begins with an extraordinary but largely forgotten moment in sporting history: the Haitian-born Joe Gaetjens scoring the goal that gave the US its famous victory over England at the 1950 World Cup. But Léger is less interested in reconstructing Gaetjens’s biography than in using the football star's journey as a " jumping point" to examining diaspora, fame, mortality and moral responsibility. Success offers neither immunity from history nor escape from mortality: as he puts it, “You could be super famous and end up on death row” or die wealthy in your own bed: “Either way, you’re going to die.

data.title: Fact-checking Trump’s speech at the United Nations General Assembly
data.description: Donald Trump’s UN address was packed with claims that are misleading, false or exaggerated. He said the US has more munitions than it could ever use, despite reports of depleting stocks. Vedika Bahl fact-checks the speech in Truth or Fake.

data.title: Holy regulation? Pope in Paris to press case for 'disarming' AI
data.description: It's all about his high holiness here in France. For weeks already, the nation's been abuzz over the upcoming visit of Leo. From Friday evening mass at Notre Dame Cathedral and mass before 600-thousand faithful in Paris to the pilgrimage city of Lourdes and a trip to Metz, hometown of father of European unity Robert Schuman. A papal visit to France usually draws much attention to the symbiotic love-hate relationship between the church and a secular state of mostly-lapsed Catholics. data.title: The long-range drone war: Ukraine and Russia scramble for supremacy in the skies
data.description: A conflict that began with tanks and then artillery is now pivoting around a new generation of drones focused on military, industrial, economic and civilian targets Finally, in the dead of night, the threat above has passed. The rain has eased and the Ukrainian drones are ready, prepared by a ground crew shrouded in hard-to-detect green and red lights. A small succession of Ukrainian Fire Point FP-2 craft, miniature monoplanes with a 6-metre wingspan and more than 100kg of explosive, line up for an attack mission into occupied Luhansk, over 200 miles away. The drone’s main piston engine is a familiar scooter’s buzz, but its launch booster is something else. The jet sound reverberates, almost painfully. A burst of fire lurches into the distance, the last of which signifies it is time for Ukraine’s 413 Raid drone regiment to pack and go. data.title: ‘My first screen kiss was in a cowshed!’ Lesley Manville on her greatest roles – and why sex scenes for over-50s are booming
data.description: In the last 15 years, she has gone from respected actor to stratospheric, garlanded star. Now she is back on TV as a chic sleuth in a racy car – despite being terrible at guessing whodunnit It is high summer and, while Lesley Manville may be suffering a bit with hay fever and the heat (“I’m so white, all I do is burn”), she doesn’t do wilting. Soon to head outside to tend to the ailing garden of her London home, she is enjoying a rare period of rest after six almost unbroken months of Oedipus on Broadway and then Les Liaisons Dangereuses at the National. She keeps, incidentally, the Tony she won for playing Jocasta in Oedipus on a shelf by the computer, “next to its friend, Larry Olivier” – an Olivier awarded for the same role. “You don’t go into a job thinking about awards,” she says, before grinning conspiratorially. “Listen, you don’t say to an Olympian, ‘Oh, is it OK that you didn’t win?’ Yes, you like to win!” Continue reading...

data.title: Labour’s last chance? The people shaping Andy Burnham’s grand plans for Britain
data.description: The new prime minister has declared he wants to end 40 years of neoliberalism. But is he really prepared to be that radical? In May 2025, when Keir Starmer was still prime minister, Labour politicians, campaigners and journalists gathered at the Ministry of Sound in London to watch a series of panel talks and presentations illuminated by the lucid glow of club lights. The day-long event was organised by a campaign group called Compass, and the subjects included child poverty, the Murdoch-owned media and the rise of the radical right. “We felt as though the Labour government was failing, and needed to be pulled into the 21st century,” Neal Lawson, the founder of Compass, told me. The Starmer government’s support for the Conservatives’ two-child benefit cap, its equivocating stance on Gaza and its emulation of far-right rhetoric – crystallised in a speech on immigration, during which the prime minister suggested Britain risked becoming an “ island of strangers ” – were causing Labour supporters to rapidly desert their party. “The Starmer project was so obviously intellectually bankrupt. He was personally so disinterested in ideas and big thinking that I thought, this is never going to fly,” Lawson said. Continue reading...

data.title: The Real Rooneys review – at least Wayne and Coleen’s reality show proves they can laugh at themselves
data.description: This trip into the celeb couple’s  Cheshire mansion is nowhere as real as they’d like you to believe. But their self-deprecation is hard not to enjoy ‘No one knows the real Rooneys,” says Coleen Rooney at the start of her family’s new reality-TV series, The Real Rooneys. “This is a side of us we’ve never shown before.” Coleen and her husband, ex-footballer Wayne, have had their personalities dissected in the tabloids every week for the past two decades; now we’re promised the truth. But how real can The Real Rooneys be? There are two obvious problems here, the first being that the Rooneys’ lives feel like fiction: he was a generational sporting talent, a one-in-a-million player whose success has bought him and Coleen a ridiculous Cheshire mansion with a cinema, indoor pool and adjacent football pitch. To get back to the road you have to drive over a bridge across a lake. As we join them, Coleen is working out how to capitalise on a recent appearance on I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, while Wayne is plotting an uptick in his media appearances that he hopes will make him a regular on Match of the Day. Technically, the Rooneys exist on our Earth, but – as they both admit, recalling their working-class childhoods in Croxteth, Liverpool – they have left ordinary life behind. Continue reading...

data.title: Abandoned, dismissed and gaslighted: there is no excuse for the way ME sufferers have been betrayed | George Monbiot
data.description: Changes in guidance and science seem to have little impact on millions of devastated lives. It’s a shocking social crisis playing out behind closed doors I’ve spent my working life covering neglected issues. But few are neglected like the devastating chronic condition ME/CFS (myalgic encephalomyelitis, or chronic fatigue syndrome). In severe cases, the illness shuts down people’s lives almost entirely, causing an extreme loss of energy and a wide range of physical and cognitive symptoms that can prevent patients from working, socialising and, sometimes, even moving or eating. Yet these people have been more or less airbrushed from our minds. To find out what this neglect looks like in practice, this week I put out a call on Bluesky asking people with ME/CFS about their recent experiences of treatment. I was immediately inundated with horrifying testimonies. “I’ve just been completely abandoned”; “a 10-year waiting list for treatment”; “we’ve given up seeking medical support”; “stuck in limbo”; “I just felt utterly unheard, invalidated”. I’ve been sent hundreds of shocking and heart-rending accounts. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: ‘And you will be the People’s Earl’ – Charles Spencer’s Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, digested by John Crace

Halley’s comet made an unscheduled appearance in the ethereal night sky. In very heaven, angelic choirs rang out. A saviour had been born. A light to lighten the world. But enough about me. For this paragraph at least. In my universally acclaimed funeral address , I aimed to speak for my sister. The real Diana. For only I truly knew her. She had the heart of a lion. And I had a glut of cliches. Yet when Diana had swept so triumphantly into the arena of royal life, I was but a callow youth awash with hormones and gripped by the self-centredness of adolescence. Nothing much has changed. Yet I know, with all my heart, that Diana would have wanted me to tell our story . Continue reading...

Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, made a presentation to the foreign ministers of the EU as well as Kenya and other countries on Wednesday night at a private meeting during the UN general assembly in New York, based on the report by the UK’s spy chiefs that found the collapse of natural systems around the world would lead to conflict, migration and food shortages. data.title: Elif Eralp: ‘Germany’s Zohran Mamdani’ who vows to be a mayor for all Berliners
data.description: Die Linke candidate, a lawyer affected by her experiences as the child of political migrants from Turkey, poised to head Berlin coalition government Elif Eralp launched her election bid last autumn with the blunt statement: “People like me are actually not supposed to become mayor in this country.” So the fact that the 45-year-old lawyer and daughter of political migrants from Turkey is on the verge of becoming Berlin’s next mayor and the capital’s first leader of Turkish origin is quite the moment in German politics. After last weekend’s city state election, in which her far-left party, Die Linke, came first with more than a quarter of the votes, Eralp has become a household name. Continue reading...

data.title: A bumper year for bugs: as the world warms up, insects are moving northwards
data.description: Britain has seen an explosion of migrating insects – in some cases from as far as northern Africa It was a stifling evening in July and Matt Phelps was out for a stroll, when a piercing, whirring noise stopped him in his tracks. As an ecologist, Phelps knows his fauna – and he could think of no UK creature that could emit such a sound. “It was like the classic sound effect of a cricket in a film, a beeping sort of little trilling sound,” said Phelps, who works at Knepp Estate in West Sussex. He returned with entomologist Graeme Lyons to track it down. But the sound, though incredibly loud, “seemed to be all around us … it was very ventriloquial”. Continue reading...

data.title: Israel facing water shortages caused by destruction of Gaza’s treatment plants
data.description: Five desalination plants shut down for days, while Gaza remains in grip of severe water and sanitation crisis Israel is facing weeks of water shortages after an exceptional algae bloom crippled much of its desalination capacity, in a crisis scientists say was triggered when Israeli attacks destroyed much of Gaza’s wastewater infrastructure, causing a massive discharge of untreated sewage. “Pollution does not recognise political borders,” said the Zalul Environmental Association, an Israeli NGO dedicated to protecting the country’s seas and shores. “The discharge of untreated sewage from the Gaza Strip into the sea is contributing to the worsening crisis affecting the Israeli desalination facilities. The wastewater contains nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, which feed microalgae and cyanobacteria and may intensify their blooms.” Continue reading...

data.title: Taking a deep dive in Helsinki’s subterranean city
data.description: Under the Finnish capital lies a world of swimming pools, go-karting tracks, playgrounds – and even an art gallery The moon is an impostor. Swimming backstroke beneath its surface, I look up at craggy hollows in close relief. White rock undulates in all directions, a forest of peaks rising next to a desert of craters. Every time I trick myself into thinking I’m somewhere celestial, the sound of children splashing brings me back to earth. This is no lunar landscape but Helsinki’s underground swimming hall, excavated from granite bedrock and officially opened in 1993. These days, Itäkeskus uimahalli is one of the Finnish capital’s most visited leisure facilities, welcoming 400,000 people a year. Local people mingle with tourists, I will discover, during a week exploring Helsinki’s subterranean metropolis. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Stranger Things was a train you can’t jump off’: Gaten Matarazzo on his return to the stage
data.description: The actor we know as Dustin was a ‘theatre kid’ from age 11. Now he’s starring in a new staging of Rent. He discusses why the musical is as relevant as ever – and what it’s like being a child star in the internet age Rent is a study in both joy and despair. The 90s rock opera spawned the kinds of irrepressible musical numbers – Seasons of Love, Take Me Or Leave Me – that would become Broadway standards, mastered and massacred in choir auditions and high schools across the world. Jonathan Larson’s self-described attempt “to bring musical theatre to the MTV generation” is also a capitalist critique: a drama about a bohemian coterie of penniless creatives sticking it to the man, all while their circle is ravaged by HIV and Aids. It still feels highly relevant today; see: What You Own – sample lyric “And when you’re living in America / At the end of the millennium / You’re what you own”. Gaten Matarazzo says “that song may arguably be more impactful now than in 1996, considering what we know about what American media and world media would become, and our access to constant mind-numbing noise …” This autumn, he makes his West End debut as Mark, the struggling film-maker who chronicles the lives of his friends in New York’s East Village, and serves as the show’s de facto narrator. Continue reading...

data.title: A Different World review – it was only a matter of time before they remade this trailblazing black sitcom
data.description: Many of the original cast of this Cosby Show-spinoff are back (including Jada Pinkett-Smith, briefly). Its look at life on a black college campus has its sights set firmly on comedy In the golden age of remaking old content and young-adult television, it was only a matter of time before a streamer got its hands on A Different World, the pioneering black sitcom that ran from 1987 to 1993 in the US. Set at a historically black college (one of a discrete group of US higher education institutions known as HBCUs), it covered issues ranging from HIV/Aids to date rape. It was a laughter-track-heavy affair that helped to pave the way for other series about upwardly mobile black Americans, among them The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air and Living Single. In any case – for reasons that will probably be abundantly clear – A Different World is an easier sell for a 2026 reboot than the programme it was an offshoot of: The Cosby Show. This new version is still steeped in the world of its predecessor (A Different-ish World?), and even boasts many members of its cast – among them Jasmine Guy, Kadeem Hardison, Darryl M Bell and Cree Summer, with a cameo from Jada Pinkett Smith. The original series ended with Dwayne (Hardison) and a pregnant Whitley (Guy) preparing to move to Tokyo; now their daughter, Deborah (Maleah Joi Moon), is attending their alma mater. (Yes, if we were following real-world time, Deborah would be in her 30s, but – from experience – it would have probably been considerably less exciting to watch a series about Deborah indulging in such thirtysomething pursuits as planning a get-together with your friends eight weeks in advance, or realising your knees have started making a weird noise every time you stand up.) Continue reading...

data.title: Mass sardine die-off pits survival of South Africa’s penguins against fishers’ livelihoods
data.description: Known as the ‘energy bars of the sea’ the fish are a key food source for many species, but closing fisheries to allow numbers to recover would cost millions It began on 28 July, when fishers near Saldanha Bay on the west coast of South Africa reported seeing dead sardines (also known as pilchards) floating at sea. Then, in early August, more dead sardines began washing up on beaches near Cape Town. In the weeks that followed, similar reports came in from places across a vast area spanning 2,600km (1,600 miles) of coastline , such as Henties Bay in Namibia and Mbotyi in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. data.title: ‘The eels were climbing out of the water to die’: why did every fish in this idyllic lake perish overnight?
data.description: Furnace Brook in East Sussex was home to carp, tench, bream, roach and trout – and 15 trailer-loads had to be buried. The mystery led to a neighbouring farm, and a story of waste, pollution and dirty rivers that reveals a lot about Britain today When Alistair and Diane Gould bought Furnace Brook in 2013, they had big plans. It was an idyllic spot: a stream-fed fishing lake nestled in a secluded valley in the High Weald, East Sussex, surrounded by woodland and fields. “People loved to come fishing here because it’s so beautiful,” says Diane. “Some of them had been coming for so many years that they got to know the individual fish.” Diane moved here from Kent in 2000, when Furnace Brook was owned by a distant relative. Her two younger sons, then 10 and 14, flourished. They would chat to the anglers about the fish they were catching and throwing back in, and sell them bacon sandwiches. Her elder son, Simon, moved from London to join them in 2006 and became a keen angler himself, and then the fishing manager, or bailiff, looking after the fish and the landscape around the lake. Continue reading...

data.title: Britain would not cut up the Bayeux tapestry. So seize this moment and reunite the Parthenon sculptures in Greece | Kyriakos Mitsotakis
data.description: Both Greek and British citizens think the sculptures should be returned. What’s needed now is political will and courage Kyriakos Mitsotakis is the prime minister of Greece For the first time in nearly 1,000 years, the Bayeux tapestry is back in Britain . Its arrival is a significant cultural moment, and a reminder that, in an age of social media and ubiquitous screens, historic objects still capture the public imagination. The British Museum describes the tapestry as one of the “wonders of the medieval world”. But the museum already houses many wonders, including one that is instantly recognisable: the Parthenon sculptures, chiselled away and illegally removed from Athens to be taken to Britain more than two centuries ago by Lord Elgin. Kyriakos Mitsotakis is the prime minister of Greece Continue reading...

data.title: The west is in freefall – and the worst part is that we were warned, but chose not to listen | Owen Jones
data.description: Endless pursuit of wealth and power by western leaders led us here. What strikes me most is how many saw what was coming The symptoms of decline are everywhere you look. On Sunday, Germany’s far right won another state election , taking nearly 40% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. France is preparing a €54bn fiscal squeeze, which could turn the screw still further on a foundering so-called European social model. At the UN general assembly, Donald Trump once again threatened to “annihilate” Iran, even as the fourth failed western war on a Muslim nation this century has added more than $100bn to Americans’ fuel bills. There is little dispute over the symptoms. The great fight of our age is over the diagnosis, and the right has been winning it for years. Its story is simple and, as the latest German state election underlines, effective: the west is dying because of migrants, Muslims, trans people, “woke” and the “deep state”. So when I told friends I was writing a book called The Fall of the West: How They Really Lost It, they worried I had shape-shifted into Liz Truss, who, after being outlasted in office by a lettuce , produced Ten Years to Save the West. Owen Jones is a Guardian columnist. His latest book, The Fall of the West: How They Really Lost It, is published on 1 October. Order your copy at the Guardian bookshop Continue reading...

data.title: Trump’s UN speech was delusional and dangerous | Kenneth Roth
data.description: It is sad and dangerous that at such a perilous moment, the United States is saddled with a president like Trump Donald Trump’s speech on Tuesday to the United Nations general assembly was an object lesson in his lawless rule and remarkable capacity for self-delusion. Disregarding the UN charter’s emphasis on the peaceful resolution of disputes, he doubled down on his violent unilateralism while denigrating the global issues that the UN is designed to address. For many, the headline remark was his musing about whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” of Iran. “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” Kenneth Roth is a Guardian US columnist, a senior fellow at Yale University and a former executive director of Human Rights Watch. He is the author of Righting Wrongs: Three Decades on the Front Lines Battling Abusive Governments Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the future of the UN: more embattled, but more necessary, than ever | Editorial
data.description: As the secretary general, António Guterres, prepares to step down, the general assembly is highlighting the scale of the organisation’s challenges The United Nations was created, its charter states , to “save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”. Donald Trump used his address to the general assembly to threaten Iran , another member state, with annihilation again. The charter also speaks of the obligations of international law. On Venezuela, Mr Trump gloated that “to the victor belong the spoils”. His speech in New York on Tuesday might be regarded as an improvement on last year’s only in that it was not an explicit, full-scale attack on the UN itself, merely on its founding principles. The absences this year are perhaps as telling as the US president’s hostile presence. Vladimir Putin has not attended for more than a decade. Nor has Xi Jinping – but the snub is more striking as he is in Washington to meet the US president. India’s Narendra Modi is not present; nor are Cyril Ramaphosa, Bola Tinubu or Abdel Fatah al-Sisi – the leaders of Africa’s three giants, South Africa, Nigeria and Egypt. While their reasons are various, the gaps speak collectively to Mr Trump’s wrecking capability and the broader challenges faced by the UN. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Netherlands v Germany: Klopp and Xavi begin revival projects with derby
data.description: Jürgen Klopp and Xavi Hernández face each other in Nations League as they take the reins following disappointing World Cups Before the latest instalment of a time-honoured international rivalry gearing up for two distinct new beginnings, Jürgen Klopp could not resist sprinkling a little of the old mischief. “The good thing is that we both have the exact same situation,” he said of Xavi Hernández, his counterpart when Germany visit the Netherlands on Thursday night. “We met on Monday and play on Thursday. And the coach knows the players from television. I actually know more of the Dutch players personally than Xavi does. Whether that’s an advantage, I don’t know, but it’s still a fact.” In his public appearances Klopp has been on irrepressible form since taking the role in July. The task of whipping Germany back into shape has visibly and audibly topped up the energy levels that had drained by the time he departed Liverpool. Klopp, his wit sharp and appetite piqued, looks a far cry from the character who, to most trained eyes, was going through the motions upon his unveiling as Red Bull’s head of global soccer early last year. Continue reading...

data.title: Florian Wirtz does not look like a £116m player but it’s too early to write him off
data.description: The 23-year-old playmaker has been disappointing for Liverpool but has he really been that bad? By Opta Analyst When Florian Wirtz signed for Liverpool in the summer of 2025, there was only one logical assumption. The Premier League champions at the time had recruited one of the hottest young talents in world football – a key player in the Bayer Leverkusen team that had won the double in 2023-24 and a star in the Germany team. An exciting and productive young attacking midfielder being added to the best team in England? How could this not work? Football has a habit of flipping the script, though. Last season was difficult for Liverpool for several reasons, and Wirtz, along with other new arrivals, struggled to make the impact expected of a player costing up to £116m. There were conversations among fans this summer about how long he and his fellow nine-figure signing Alexander Isak should be given before difficult questions needed be asked. The consensus was until Christmas. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s not in us’: Anthony Gordon backs Tuchel over England’s possession problem
data.description: Barcelona winger says England cannot play like Spain Gordon: players ‘could have done more’ in semi-final Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA. Although Gordon revealed surprise at being substituted when England were 1-0 up in their World Cup semi-final against Argentina , the winger refused to blame the defeat on Tuchel’s decisions and argued that wider cultural issues influenced the side’s collapse. England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA. Continue reading...

data.title: UK ‘losing up to £6.5bn a year in EU trade’ without post-Brexit product deal
data.description: IPPR finds failure to align testing standards has forced companies to abandon exporting to EU and is costing costing 0.18% of national income The UK is losing out on annual exports to the EU that could be worth as much as £6.5bn without a deal with Brussels that allows manufacturers to jettison duplicate product testing. In the latest attempt to calculate the loss of trade with the EU after Brexit, the IPPR thinktank said many companies have given up selling goods to the EU or set up subsidiaries inside the trade bloc after successive governments failed to secure a mutual recognition agreement that would avoid the extra administration costs. Motor vehicle and part exports would have been between £2.48bn and £3.42bn higher each year. Electronic exports could have been between £1.17bn and £1.67bn higher. Pharmaceutical exports would have had an estimated annual uplift of between £740m and £820m. Continue reading...

data.title: UK interest rates ‘increasingly likely to rise’ if energy prices remain high, Bank of England’s Lombardelli warns – business live
data.description: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news Newsflash: A Bank of England deputy governor is warning that interest rates will be raised, if necessary, to combat the risk of persistent inflationary pressures from higher oil prices. Clare Lombardelli is telling the Sixth Biennial Conference on Macroeconomic Policy in Warsaw that the energy shock due to the conflict in the Middle East is likely to keep pushing UK inflation higher in the coming months. Strong demand for AI components is already pushing up global export prices and weather-related shocks add upside risks. On the other hand, trade diversion is reducing inflation. The longer higher energy prices persist, the greater the risk that indirect effects build and that inflation expectations, wage bargaining and price-setting behaviour begin to adjust in response. On that basis, policy is increasingly likely to need to tighten if elevated energy prices persist, absent clear evidence of disinflation or weaker activity. But this is by no means suggesting that monetary policy should respond mechanically to movements in energy prices. The key issue is not the spot price of energy itself but the interaction of the underlying economy, higher energy prices, and the nature of their transmission. That, ultimately, is what will determine whether Bank Rate needs to rise. Continue reading...

data.title: Bats originated in Europe, rewriting mammals’ family tree, study reveals
data.description: Biggest study of its kind provides insights into bats’ evolution – a potential gamechanger for research into treating viruses and cancer in humans In the northern forests of the Congo-Brazzaville, as the sun slips away, a distinctive honking fills the dusky sky. Every evening, thousands of hammer-headed fruit bats depart their daytime roosts in search of mates, calling out through large, box-shaped snouts that give the flying mammals the appearance of a winged moose. Here, along the Congo River, scientists have been collecting DNA swabs and tissue samples from the bats for years, working deep into the night in spacesuit-like protective gear. Those hard-won samples are now among the thousands of specimens gathered from bats across the world that have helped to reshape what we know about the bat family tree. Continue reading...

data.title: Forgotten Island review – best friends forever trapped in frantic DreamWorks animation
data.description: This over-controlled adventure never takes a breath or a moment to let its characters come to life Frantically and even stroboscopically over-energised, this big new movie from DreamWorks about best friends for ever seems to me another example of exhausting AI-type content production in animation. You could make the same argument against plenty of live-action films of course, but it is in animation that this kind of soulless blitzkrieg tends to predominate. Forgotten Island is over-controlled and over-determined, a movie that never, or hardly ever, takes its pedal from the metal, never takes a breath or a moment to let its characters come to life. At times it seems to be aping the world of Japanese anime, but without its sense of character or capacity for calm. The story, weirdly reminiscent of The Hangover of all things, is set in the Philippines in the pre-social media 90s. Jo, voiced by R&B star HER, is a lonely and super-imaginative teen always in trouble at school; like Moana she has a wise grandma who guides her to her ancestral destiny and has captivated Jo with stories of her culture and identity – stories of the forgotten island of Nakali. Jo makes friends with similarly lonely Raissa (Liza Soberano) who like Jo is smart but with a much more focused sense of academic discipline. Continue reading...

data.title: Manhunter review – Michael Mann serves up a bold and queasy starter to the serial killer spectacle
data.description: Before Anthony Hopkins’ Dr Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs, Brian Cox played a cannibalistic killer in Mann’s pioneering Red Dragon adaptation Five years before The Silence of the Lambs, there was writer-director Michael Mann’s pioneering Thomas Harris adaptation Manhunter, now on re-release in a director’s “final cut” for its 40th anniversary. It was his version of Harris’s 1981 novel Red Dragon, a movie which features Dr Hannibal Lecter (here spelt Lecktor) in a relatively minor part, and played in a much more coolly matter-of-fact and downbeat way by Brian Cox, who is first discovered in his cell lying down with his back to the camera. It has long been a haughty, hipster film-bro affectation to claim that Cox is better in the role than Anthony Hopkins. (Lecktor’s early acoustic stuff was great, you see, before he went electric as Lecter.) I think that’s a bit obtuse, for all that Cox is of course very good. Hopkins in The Silence of the Lambs is the definitive version: face it. But I will concede that Cox is more interesting than Hopkins by the time the latter came to make the 2002 adaptation of Red Dragon, at which stage the franchise had become a bit tired. Manhunter itself is a very interesting and watchable movie, but feels a little unevolved compared to Jonathan Demme’s masterly guignol spectacle, although Demme clearly inhaled Mann’s excitement at jets, ’copters and military hardware deployed at speed to bring down just one man. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s about being loudly visible’: Ahadadream, the British-Pakistani dance star defanging racist slurs
data.description: Like many south Asians in the UK, he kept creativity separate from a corporate career. But after co-signs from dance music’s A-list, he’s releasing a defiant – and daringly titled – debut album When Ahad Elley was 12, his family moved from Karachi to the UK. Quickly, he discovered his Pakistani identity was the basis of a slur. “Growing up in Pakistan, I never knew that was a bad word, because why would it be? The word ‘pak’ means clean, it has no negative connotations.” Elley’s childhood response was to disconnect from his heritage, and what followed was “potentially shrinking or hiding parts of myself to fit into society”. It’s likely a familiar story for many diasporic south Asians who, at some point, have felt the call to assimilate. Twenty years later, Elley is better known as Ahadadream, an integral architect of the current British south Asian music scene, as well as a DJ, producer, label head, A&R and promoter shining a light on dance music from around the world. His tracks are favourites in sets by A-list dance artists such as Fred Again, Caribou, Peggy Gou and Four Tet, and with the release of his debut album, P★KI (pronounced “pee-star-kay-eye”) Elley’s star is set to rise further. Continue reading...

data.title: Exit Party by Emily St John Mandel review – alternate visions of post-crisis America
data.description: Is the price of stability necessarily the loss of freedom? Two possible future worlds are linked in the new novel from the author of Station Eleven In her second novel, 2009’s The Singer’s Gun, Emily St John Mandel tells the story of Anton Waker, a young man desperate to make a break from his criminal family. His plans are thwarted by his cousin Ari, whose hard-nosed talent for operating outside the law has become a way of life. A decade later in The Glass Hotel , a painting called Swan Dive that hangs in the lobby of the luxury retreat stands as a symbol of escape from a trap that is closing. You will not need to have read either of these earlier novels to enjoy Mandel’s seventh, Exit Party, though their loose intertwining of narrative threads will provide extra pleasure and a sense of homecoming for those who have. It is also interesting to observe Mandel’s evolution from a writer of quirky tales of offbeat protagonists to a novelist whose world-spanning, politically resonant narratives now attract a wide and devoted following. Exit Party begins five years into our future, in 2031. Ari Waker has just come out of prison after serving an 18-year sentence for the attempted murder by contract killing of her cousin Anton. Much has changed while she has been inside: a second civil war has devastated lives and blighted the economy, and the United States as such has ceased to exist. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Why no female lead characters this year?’: The Guardian’s book team answered your questions
data.description: This year’s shortlist for the Booker prize was announced last night. Our books editors answered your questions about the contenders, the judges and literary fiction Kohtao says: Can’t believe the two best books – Switzy and Shadow of the Object - were cut. Huge shame as they really added something different to the range. Liese: I was sad not to see Switzy on the shortlist too. I am a big fan of Emma Cline’s writing and felt that it did something really interesting. I am sure that, as always, there were plenty of arguments and some horse-trading among the judges to arrive at this list – which does still include ambitious and experimental work such as The Disappearers (Marlon James) and one of my other faves, the brilliantly weird Black Bag. Charlotte: It’s interesting that even Jarvis Cocker, one of this year’s judges, said that he found the male dominance of the list “quite surprising, because generally speaking the male-written books weren’t as good as the ones written by women”. And it’s also surprising in the light of the recent debate around the lack of contemporary novels written by men – there was even a small press, Conduit Books , established last year to focus on new male writers. So perhaps we could say that’s succeeded! But in fact, a lot of the men on the list are very long established, and there are two previous winners among them – Marlon James and Douglas Stuart. I would say that although the perspectives are predominantly male, they’re not necessarily similar in other ways – they encompass different sexualities, and as you say, one isn’t gendered at all (funnily enough, I hadn’t read it that way, but others on the desk did and that’s obviously how it was intended). It’s interesting that we have a female author, Elizabeth Strout , writing from a male perspective, and a male author, M John Harrison, writing from a female perspective. Though Harrison’s novel isn’t entirely from Marnie’s perspective, and for me there are many other themes that jump out from these books, beyond masculinity – anxiety about the world and the future, sexuality, history, oppression. As a shortlist, it seems pretty varied to me, and I didn’t find that I missed a female perspective when I was reading these books. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m a writer but then nobody’s perfect’: how Billy Wilder conquered Hollywood
data.description: From émigré roots to a titan of modern cinema, penning classics such as Double Indemnity, Some Like It Hot and The Apartment, a new retrospective celebrates the father of film noir’s incredible career Like all survivors, Billy Wilder never forgot where he came from or what he had left behind. He was born at the start of the 20th century in Austria-Hungary and died at the start of the 21st in California, the inscription on his gravestone a nod to his most famous line: “I’m a writer but then nobody’s perfect.” Wilder, though, had a habit of of making flawless films throughout his career, a point proved by Almost Perfect, a comprehensive retrospective of his work, running at the BFI Southbank from 19 October until the end of the year. Wilder was an inveterate self-mythologiser, a film-maker with a brand long before there were opportunities for promotion through Instagram accounts and chicken shop dates. He told a story of living in Berlin during his fledgling years in show business and being kept awake all night by “a toilet that was on the blink”. Continue reading...

data.title: A blood-splattered surgeon after an emergency horse op: Andrea Modica’s best photograph
data.description: ‘You’d have to be out of your mind not to want to photograph this incredible woman. And it was only afterwards that I realised she looks like a medieval statue, a madonna’ After my first job in the 80s, I had a little money and set off for Italy with my camera and a backpack. I had grown up hearing about Italy, where my family is from, and so began 40 years of travelling back and forth – at times to teach photography, or for a relationship, and always to make photographs with no real agenda, just being in the moment. My new book and the show that this image appears in spans my many visits. It was taken about six years ago. I became very interested in a horse hospital outside Bologna. I made a large body of work there and this first appeared in a book called Theatrum Equorum, Latin for Horse Theatre, all caught on an old-style large-format 8x10 camera. Continue reading...

data.title: Australia banned this anti-fascist play in 1936 at the request of the Nazis. Ninety years on, it’s being staged again
data.description: A new production of Clifford Odets’ agitprop work Till the Day I Die is being remounted on the back of a truck in a Melbourne car park – rekindling its activist intent It might be difficult to imagine these days, but there was a time when theatre in Australia was so politically incendiary it could cause an international diplomatic scandal. A year after it premiered on Broadway in 1935, US playwright Clifford Odets ’ Till the Day I Die found itself at the centre of controversy in Australia when it was banned by the federal government at the request of the Nazi party’s consul general, on the grounds it was offensive to a “friendly foreign nation”. Odets’ play, about a communist Berliner arrested by the Nazis for producing leftwing political pamphlets, was a companion piece to his more famous Waiting for Lefty, which was staged the year before by Sydney’s New Theatre – one of a branch of theatre companies that sprang up around the globe in the 1930s that was heavily affiliated with communism. The ban was counterproductive, leading to a massive public outcry and a cobbled, surreptitious production performed on the back of a truck at Collingwood town hall in Melbourne. That truck is a galvanising symbol of rebellion and resistance for theatre-makers Mark Wilson and Katie Sfetkidis, who have been inspired to revisit the play as an act of leftist solidarity with the past and a spur for future activism. They’re staging a new production of it for this year’s Melbourne fringe festival in the car park of the Trades Hall building on the back of their own truck. “We got excited by these artists refusing to be banned, about the idea of a necessary theatre,” Wilson says. Continue reading...

data.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for tomatoes stuffed with breadcrumbs, chickpeas and herbs | A kitchen in Rome
data.description: A well-seasoned and comforting meal to ease you into the autumn months At this time of year, baked tomatoes stuffed with rice and surrounded by a packing-chip sea of potatoes are typical all over central and southern Italy, and in many other places besides. So much so that when I see a tray of those wrinkled red caps in a bakery or canteen-like tavola calda (literally, “hot table”), it doesn’t cross my mind that the hollowed-out tomatoes underneath might be filled with something other than rice. It was only when the woman behind the counter was wrapping my two portions of cannelloni and four slices of margherita pizza that another person’s order alerted me to the fact that these tomatoes were in fact filled with breadcrumbs, chickpeas, sausage, cheese and herbs. Suddenly, the tomatoes were the most appealing item behind the steamed-up glass, and the only thing I could want. We were in Tavola Calda in Latina , just south of Rome, during the lunchtime rush, which is why I didn’t feel able to add to my order, but then I was dissatisfied with my lunch. But dissatisfaction gave me a reason to pull Claudia Roden’s A Book of Middle Eastern Food from the shelf, for her chapter dedicated to stuffed vegetables, which draws inspiration from Turkish, Uzbekistani, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Greek, Egyptian, Persian, Syrian, Lebanese, Saudi Arabian and north African recipes. Having noted that almost any vegetable can be stuffed, Roden adds that the most common filling for a hollowed-out vegetable is a well-seasoned mix of chopped onion, minced meat, rice, chopped parsley, and maybe chopped tomato; and she then goes on to give seven filling variations – some with rice, some with meat (no pork), and with various herbs and spices. She also provides a not disappointing filling including chickpeas, which is what I have adapted, also with inspiration from the busy Tavola Calda, for this week’s recipe. Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: in praise of slightly silly clothes
data.description: The push to buy lasting, sustainable clothes is a good thing, but every wardrobe need a bit of mischief I do hope you are wearing your zebra stripe trousers today. Anyone who is anyone is wearing zebra stripes this month, you know. If you haven’t yet got with the programme, I suggest you nip to the shops and snap some up before they are all gone. It would be mortifying to be the last one without a pair. Hurry! Only teasing. Fashion doesn’t work like that any more. The days when people like me bullied everyone else into wearing banana yellow one season and puffball sleeves the next are over. Looking trendy is over. Timeless chic is the only show in town. Peacocking has been phased out in favour of understatement and personal style. Continue reading...

data.title: Something in your eye? Here’s how to get it out – without making it worse
data.description: It’s natural to want to soothe eye irritation, but mishandling could lead to more problems, experts warn. We asked them for advice on how to deal with it properly It may feel like a gritty, annoying sensation, or a sharp pain. Either way, you may have the same problem: something is stuck in your eye and needs to come out. Addressing the situation incorrectly can lead to bigger issues such as infection, scarring, an ulcer or corneal scratches, which are abrasions on the clear covering of your eye. Ignoring the dilemma can lead to similar consequences. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I miss old Google’: readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI
data.description: A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting. “AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” wrote Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, last August . In May, the company said more AI is coming . Continue reading...

data.title: ‘This is where I live now, the back of a truck’: a day in the life of a grandmother in Gaza
data.description: As the war in Gaza approaches its fourth year, the Guardian follows five ordinary Palestinians as they go about their lives. Each tells the story of their day, revealing the terrible toll of the conflict. At 76, Mansoura’s most precious possession is the key to her former home As the war in Gaza approaches its fourth year, this week, the Guardian follows five ordinary Palestinians as they go about their lives. Each will tell the story of their day, revealing the terrible toll of the ongoing conflict. The flat-bed truck is open to the hot summer air, its metal frame covered on two sides by draped tarpaulins, the rear by a pegged-up bedsheet. On the tin floor lies a squab mattress and pillow with a yellow frilled cover. Last night, I stayed awake until 2 am. I barely sleep during the night because of the mosquitoes and the heat. I fall asleep for a short while, I wake up early in the morning, pray to God, and wait to hear the call to dawn prayer. When I wake up, I call for my grandson to bring over the white plastic chair that I need to climb in and out of the truck. Continue reading...

data.title: Eight USS Lincoln personnel have attempted suicide, US navy confirms
data.description: Hung Cao, acting US navy secretary, answered questions from US senator Kirsten Gillibrand in a letter Eight US navy personnel assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group have attempted suicide since the start of their lengthy deployment as part of the US war on Iran, Hung Cao, the acting US navy secretary, revealed in a letter to the US senator Kirsten Gillibrand on Tuesday. “Since the beginning of Lincoln’s deployment, there have been a total of eight suicide attempts across the strike group,” Cao wrote, responding on behalf of US defense secretary Pete Hegseth to Gillibrand’s inquiry about the quality of life aboard the fleet. “This number includes the Lincoln crew and sailors from the carrier airwing, strike group and destroyer squadron staff, escorting destroyers and all embarked aviation squadrons.” Continue reading...

data.title: Viajar para caminhar e pensar: o que isso nos ensina?
data.description: Quilômetros de caminhada , paisagens espetaculares, músculos doloridos e muito tempo para pensar. Numa travessia, a jornada começa em um ponto e termina em outro, cruzando dunas, serras, vales ou montanhas ao longo de vários dias. Embora a palavra esteja desgastada como metáfora, aqui ela recupera seu sentido literal e simbólico: quem se propõe a andar por horas a fio realmente atravessa desafios importantes, físicos e mentais. Leia mais (09/24/2026 - 04h00)

data.title: Dödade sina barn – stöttas världen över
data.description: En januaridag för tre år sedan tar Lindsay Clancy ner sina tre barn i källaren. Medan maken är iväg för att köpa hämtmat, stryper hon dem ett efter ett. I rättegången, som äger rum nu i år, hävdar hennes försvarare att hon hade drabbats av en förlossningsspsykos och inte kan hållas rättsligt ansvarig. Den sidan har fått stöd av hundratusentals, i huvudsak mammor, på sociala medier. Samtidigt ser andra Lindsay Clancy som ett monster som måste straffas hårt. Hur kan bilden av morden skilja sig så mycket åt?

data.title: Två oligarker splittrar EU:s enighet om ryska sanktioner

data.title: Experten: Almgren är unik i friidrottshistorien

data.title: Stała baza USA w Polsce. Wiceszefowa MON potwierdza doniesienia „Rz” o możliwym terminie
data.description: Decyzja w sprawie stałej bazy USA w Polsce może zapaść pod koniec roku – informowała we wtorek „Rzeczpospolita”. Teraz doniesienia te potwierdziła wiceszefowa MON Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka. Jak zaznaczyła, wcześniej powinna zapaść decyzja w sprawie ewentualnego powstania w Polsce centrum serwisowego rakiet do systemów Patriot.

data.title: Kam si jen odskočit... New York instaluje nová WC. Přetáhnete? Otevřou se
data.description: Najít v New Yorku veřejnou toaletu je překvapivě složité. Město s více než osmi miliony obyvatel jich má totiž jen necelou tisícovku. Radnice proto začala s instalací nových modulárních toalet. Jsou bezplatné, klimatizované a bezdotykové. Na pobyt v oné místnosti máte ovšem striktně vyhrazený čas.

data.title: Srážku vlaků s 37 zraněnými zavinil strojvůdce rychlíku, škoda je nakonec poloviční
data.description: Listopadovou čelní srážku vlaků Českých drah u Zlivi na Českobudějovicku zavinil podle zjištění Drážní inspekce strojvedoucí rychlíku, který projel návěstidlo s příkazem stůj. Při nehodě se zranilo 37 lidí a celková škoda byla vyčíslena na 85,2 milionu korun.

data.title: Sociální byty ano, ale tak aby nevznikla nová ghetta, tvrdí lídr SPD
data.description: Narodil se na Slovensku, po rozdělení Československa přijal české občanství. Plzeň považuje za pohodové místo pro život, jen by tu podle něj měl být větší pořádek. Řeč je o lídrovi kandidátky SPD, Trikolory, PRO a Přísahy pro nadcházející komunální volby v Plzni Júliu Líškovi. „Důležitější než stavět cyklostezky nebo rozhledny je dávat peníze na sociálně slabší lidi,“ říká.

data.title: Byly v kauze Epstein mezi oběťmi i Češky?  Policie zveřejnila výsledky šetření
data.description: Česká policie svým šetřením nezjistila, že by mezi oběťmi amerického finančníka a sexuálního delikventa Jeffreyho Epsteina byly i ženy z Česka, uvedl ve čtvrtek mluvčí policejního prezidia Jakub Vinčálek. data.title: Ve Walesu se zřítil letoun britského letectva, dopadl poblíž domů
data.description: Cvičný letoun britského královského letectva (RAF) se ve středu zřítil a explodoval v blízkosti vesnických domů na severu Walesu. Video zachycující havárii ukazuje, že se dvojice pilotů katapultovala těsně před tím, než se stroj Hawk T2 zřítil kolmo k zemi. Piloty lékaři ošetřili s lehkými zraněními, nikomu dalšímu se nic nestalo. Příčina nehody zatím není známa.

data.title: Po rekonstrukci za miliardy ožívá Průmyslový palác. Zcela nové je levé křídlo zničené požárem
data.description: Po čtyřleté rekonstrukci se otevřel Průmyslový palác na pražském Výstavišti. Část dominanty Holešovic zničil v roce 2008 požár, oprava ale začala až v roce 2022. Měla skončit už loni, ale kvůli zjištěnému horšímu stavu se protáhla. Veřejnost si bude moci palác prohlédnout od pátku při komentovaných prohlídkách.

data.title: Kdy přijedete do Moskvy? Na raketě, odpálil Zelenskyj ruského reportéra
data.description: Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj se v New Yorku dostal do slovní přestřelky s ruským televizním reportérem. Když se ho novinář Všeruské státní televizní a rozhlasové společnosti (VGTRK) Valentin Bogdanov několikrát zeptal, kdy přijede do Moskvy, Zelenskyj mu odpověděl: „Na raketě.“ Podle záznamu přitom zřejmě přidal i vulgární výraz.

data.title: V Česku operuje náhrada za Sputnik, varuje BIS. Mluví pro ni Rajchl i Majerová
data.description: Desítky milionů zhlédnutí a tisíce fanoušků. Internetová stránka neČT24, jež je především aktivní na sociálních sítích, je podle Bezpečnostní informační služby (BIS) přímo napojená na ruský státní aparát. Stránce, která je podle tajných služeb nástupcem zakázaného Sputniku, pravidelně poskytují rozhovory přední čeští politici. Na svém počínání nevidí nic nevhodného.

data.title: Soud propustil dezinformátora Čermáka. Překopal jsem svou osobnost, tvrdí
data.description: Soud podmínečně propustil Tomáše Čermáka, který si odpykával 5,5 roku vězení v rýnovické věznici za podporu a propagaci terorismu. Okresní soud v Liberci vyhověl jeho žádosti ve čtvrtek dopoledne. Čermák dostal pravomocný trest za video, v němž se vymezoval proti opatřením proti pandemii covidu-19 a proti novele pandemického zákona. Za sebou má už více než polovinu uloženého trestu.

data.title: V Plané nad Lužnicí shořela hala s kamiony i ropnými látkami. Propadla se střecha
data.description: V Plané nad Lužnicí ráno shořela hala, v níž byla mimo jiné i nákladní auta. Budově se propadla střecha. Hasiči vyhlásili druhý stupeň poplachu ze čtyř, informovali o tom na síti X. data.title: Soudce zvrátil Trumpův zákaz. CNN, MS NOW a Politico se mohou vrátit do Bílého domu

data.title: Na silnice máme peněz dost, říká ŘSD. Hlavní cíl je dokončení páteřní dálniční sítě
data.description: Ředitelství silnic a dálnic (ŘSD) plánuje v následujících patnácti měsících zahájit stavbu nových 90,8 kilometru dálnic, 50,3 kilometru silnic první třídy a zvýšit kapacitu zhruba třináct kilometrů dálnic. Mezi nimi jsou úseky dálnice D52 před Novomlýnskými nádržemi, úseky D6 u Karlových Varů, část D7 u Postoloprt nebo úseky D55 mezi Kokory a Přerovem a mezi Napajedly a Babicemi.

data.title: Pruhy pro auta jsou často zbytečně široké, míní lídryně Zelených v Brně
data.description: Z celostátního pohledu patří Zelení spíš k okrajovému politickému proudu, ačkoliv díky společné kandidatuře s Piráty mají po 15 letech dnes i své poslankyně. Nicméně v Brně je tato strana stálicí téměř nepřetržitě od roku 1990. Poslední období si její političky hodně berou na mušku automobilovou dopravu a chování některých řidičů, kteří odstaví auto, kde se jim zlíbí.

data.title: Turkiye to transfer Bashiqa base to Iraq under phased troop withdrawal agreement

The agreement also includes Iraqi commitments to address armed groups in the Sinjar region that Turkiye has identified as security threats, according to the statement. The development coincides with the United States’ planned end to its military presence in Iraq, as reported by US officials.

data.title: Saudi Embassy in Georgia hosts reception to mark National Day
data.description: The Saudi Embassy in Georgia hosted a reception in the capital, Tbilisi, to mark National Day, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Wednesday. Saudi Ambassador to Georgia Salman Al-Sheikh welcomed Georgian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Alexander Khvtisiashvili, ambassadors from friendly countries and Georgian government officials. Embassy staff and Saudi students studying in Georgia also attended the reception.

data.title: El desahucio de una jubilada de 87 años en silla de ruedas expone la crisis de vivienda en España
data.description: Maricarmen Abascal, una jubilada de 87 años, no pudo salir por su propio pie de una vivienda que ocupaba en Madrid desde que tenía 16. Confinada a una silla de ruedas, tuvo media hora para reunir sus pertenencias esenciales antes de ser desalojada en camilla por policías que ejecutaban un desahucio ordenado por un tribunal. El caso de la octogenaria ha vuelto a poner de relieve el drama inmobiliario de España.

data.title: ¿Es costoso construir y reparar edificaciones en Venezuela?
data.description: Construir edificaciones sismorresistentes en Venezuela no es opcional, se trata de una exigencia legal de acuerdo con la norma Covenin 1756, lo que incrementa los costos de diseño y obra. Ante el colapso industrial de cemento y acero, el sector depende de insumos importados y de costosos diagnósticos técnicos para adecuar viejas estructuras. data.title: Kégué, le 25 septembre : chronique d’une vigilance amoureuse.
data.description:
Il est des veilles de bataille où le fracas des tambours se tait au profit d'un murmure. C'est dans cette tonalité feutrée, presque sacrée, que nous parvient le souffle de Lomé. 
 À l'orée de cette confrontation tant attendue entre les Éperviers du Togo et les Intamba Mu Rugamba du Burundi, prévue le 25 septembre 2026 dans l'écrin brûlant du Stade de Kégué, nos hôtes ont choisi la noblesse du verbe plutôt que l'outrance du défi.

data.title: Lomé, veillée d’armes : le Général est là
data.description:
Ce n'était plus un simple entraînement. Sous le ciel écrasant de Lomé, c'était une veillée d'armes. Une poignée d'hommes qui répétaient leurs gammes avant le grand saut de Kégué, ce 25 septembre. 
 Et au milieu de cette tension noble, est apparu le Président de la Fédération de Football du Burundi, le Général de Brigade de Police Muyenge Alexandre.

data.title: Cameroun/ présidence du MRC : Brice Ronnic Djolako se retire et appelle à voter Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah
data.description: © DR Premier à avoir déposé sa candidature à la succession de Maurice Kamto, Brice Ronnic Djolako annonce le 23 septembre son retrait de la course à la présidence nationale et le retrait de sa liste. La succession de Maurice Kamto connaît son premier rebondissement majeur. Dans un message adressé aux délégués, Brice Ronnic Djolako, le fédéraliste autoproclamé "Cardinal du pape KAMTO" appelle désormais à soutenir l’actuelle présidente nationale par intérim, pour la convention d’octobre prochain. "J'annonce le retrait de ma candidature au poste de président National du MRC ainsi que celle de ma liste et j'appelle à voter pour la Candidate Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah." Un retrait total. Une candidature déposée en premier, retirée en premier. Le calendrier est important. Le 16 septembre, date de clôture des dépôts, trois listes avaient été enregistrées au siège national du MRC à Yaoundé. Celle de Brice Ronnic Djolako (avec Janvier Tamesse comme 1er vice-président et François Ayissi au Secrétariat Général). La liste de Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah. Et la liste de Pierre Emmanuel Binyam qui a connu un réaménagement récent. Djolako avait été le premier à se lancer, mais avec une liste incomplète - un poste de vice-président n'avait pas été pourvu. Une semaine plus tard, il est le premier à se retirer, et son ralliement est clair et stratégique. En appelant les délégués à voter pour Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah, Djolako fait basculer le rapport de force interne à trois semaines de la convention. La compétition pour la succession de Maurice Kamto et de Mamadou Yacouba Mota, dont les démissions ont été annoncées le 8 septembre, se jouera donc désormais entre deux listes : Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah, désormais soutenue par Djolako et Pierre Emmanuel Binyam. Un duel qui s'annonce serré pour la convention extraordinaire élective programmée le 17 octobre 2026 au siège du parti à Yaoundé. En signant son message de retrait, Djolako rappelle sa loyauté à Maurice Kamto tout en actant la fin de son ambition présidentielle interne. Reste à savoir si ce ralliement entraînera un report massif des voix de sa base vers la candidate Noah. Cet article Cameroun/ présidence du MRC : Brice Ronnic Djolako se retire et appelle à voter Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ Enseignement supérieur : le ministre Fame Ndongo désamorce la fronde des personnels d’appui
data.description: © DR Le ministre d'Etat, ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur, Jacques Fame Ndongo, a reçu le 23 septembre à 16h le bureau du Syndicat national des personnels d’appui des universités d’État –Synapauc-. La rencontre entre les parties s'inscrit dans le dialogue social et s'est tenue en présence d'un représentant du ministère des Finances -Minfi-, des recteurs des universités de Yaoundé I et II. Au cœur des échanges, les revendications historiques des personnels d'appui. Il s’agit entre autres du profil de carrière, de la grille salariale, des rappels et avancements bloqués, les assurances et la fluidité des salaires. Les échanges ont porté sur les différents points et ont conduit les parties vers la résolution définitive desdites revendications. D’après le communique du ministre d’Etat ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur Minesup, les solutions ont été classées par temporalité (court et moyen terme) et par responsabilité (Universités, Minesup, Minfi). Un chronogramme d'actions a été adopté et un comité de suivi incluant toutes les parties a été créé pour veiller à son exécution. En retour, le Synapauc a salué la création en 2012 de la Division du dialogue et de la solidarité universitaire, et a réaffirmé sa loyauté au Chef de l’État et au Premier ministre Joseph Dion Ngute, en s'engageant à préserver la sérénité du climat social dans les campus. Un dialogue à l'ombre de la grève enseignante Cette main tendue intervient dans un contexte particulièrement tendu pour le système éducatif camerounais. Le Minesup tente d'éteindre un foyer de contestation dans le supérieur, marque par la grève des enseignants qui revendiquent le paiement intégral de la dette académique accumulée entre 2000 et 2021 et dont le montant à apurer est 9,696 milliards, soit 57% de la dette totale. Alors que les ministres concernés mobilisent des fonds pour apaiser les tensions en commençant par régler les arriérés des primes de la modernisation de la recherche , il n’est pas question qu’un autre front complique la situation. Pour le gouvernement, l'enjeu est donc double : éviter que la grogne des personnels d'appui ne vienne s'ajouter à celle des enseignants et ne conduise à une paralysie totale à quelques semaines de la rentrée académique 2026-2027. En désamorçant le front du Synapauc par le dialogue, le ministre Fame Ndongo tente de préserver au moins le climat social dans les universités. Cet article Cameroun/ Enseignement supérieur : le ministre Fame Ndongo désamorce la fronde des personnels d’appui est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Gaz domestique au Cameroun : la stratégie du gouvernement pour gérer la rareté
data.description: © DR Pour faire face à la pénurie de gaz parfois créée par certains acteurs pour favoriser la spéculation sur les prix, le gouvernement adopte une nouvelle stratégie de gestion. Elle vise à neutraliser les tricheurs et tous les obstacles identifiés afin de fluidifier la distribution. Dans les quartiers de Yaoundé, Douala, Garoua ou Bafoussam, la scène est la même : des ménagères qui parcourent des kilomètres avec leur bouteille de 12,5 kg sur la tête ou sur la moto à la recherche du précieux sésame. Quand une station-service annonce avoir du gaz, c'est la ruée, parfois les bousculades. Pourtant, le gaz existe dans la chaîne. Il arrive au port. Il est stocké à la SCDP. Mais il n'arrive pas dans les points de vente. Le diagnostic du ministre de l’Eau et de l’Energie –Minee- est sans appel : la rareté est organisée. La lettre circulaire du 23 septembre 2026, signée par le ministre Gaston Eloundou Essomba lève le voile sur 3 mécanismes qui assèchent le marché. D’abord le blocage des fonds. Certains marketers ne paient pas les importateurs dans les délais. Résultat, l'importateur bloque la prochaine cargaison. Paralyse tout le marché. Ensuite, le détournement du produit. Le gaz subventionné par l'État pour les ménages (6 500 F la bouteille) est revendu illégalement aux industries à prix fort. Plus rentable pour le marketer, insupportable pour les ménages. Enfin, le privilège réservé aux gros clients.  Au lieu de livrer les dépôts de quartiers, certains opérateurs enlèvent tout pour livrer une seule industrie qui paie cash. Les points de vente restent vides. Ces pratiques "privent les ménages de cette source d'énergie vitale et sont susceptibles de créer des troubles à l'ordre public", avertit le ministre pour dire que cela doit cesser. La gestion de la rareté en 5 leviers Après une concertation de plus de 3 heures vendredi dernier avec tous les acteurs, le Minee ne gère plus la rareté en la subissant. Il la gère en la corrigeant à la source. Il entend tout d’abord sécuriser les arrivages par le respect strict du calendrier prévisionnel des livraisons par les importateurs. A cet effet, à en croire le membre du gouvernement, il n’y aura plus de cargaison de gaz en retard qui crée un trou de deux semaines dans le stock. Ensuite, il s’agit de fluidifier l’argent par l’obligation de paiement des factures dans les délais contractuels. L’autre levier est d’imposer l’équité qui veut que la SCDP repartisse les cargaisons selon parts de marché et les contrats. Ce qui tend à mettre fin à la mesure "premier arrivé, premier servi" qui avantage les tricheurs. L’avant dernier levier veut placer le Cameroun en priorité. Les importations destinées au marché national passent en priorité. Le transit vers le Tchad et la RCA ne doit plus pénaliser le marché local. Il reste que la mesure soit suivie d’une application immédiate et effective. data.title: Mémorandum d’Abuja : l’Autorité portuaire nationale engagée à Libreville pour la sécurité maritime
data.description: © DR L'Autorité portuaire nationale (APN) prend part depuis le 21 septembre 2026 à Libreville à la 16e Réunion du Comité de Contrôle des Navires par l'État du Port et à la 6e Conférence ministérielle du Mémorandum d'Abuja. Une participation conduite par Mme Raïssa Lindjeke pour renforcer la sécurité maritime et la conformité des navires dans l'espace régional. Le Cameroun au cœur de la sécurité maritime africaine. L'Autorité Portuaire Nationale (APN) prend une part active aux travaux consacrés au renforcement de la sécurité maritime et du contrôle des navires dans l'espace couvert par le Mémorandum d'Abuja. Conduite par Madame Raïssa Lindjeke, Chef de la Division des affaires juridiques et du contentieux, la délégation camerounaise participe depuis le 21 septembre 2026, au Palais des Congrès Omar Bongo Ondimba de Libreville, à deux rencontres majeures : la 16e Réunion du Comité de Contrôle des Navires par l'État du Port (PSCC16) et la 6e Conférence ministérielle du Mémorandum d'Abuja. Ces assises constituent une plateforme de concertation entre les États membres sur les défis liés au contrôle des navires par l'État du port, à la sûreté de la navigation et à la protection de l'environnement marin. Les travaux portent notamment sur le renforcement des mécanismes de coopération, l'amélioration des dispositifs de contrôle et l'identification d'actions communes en faveur d'une meilleure conformité des navires opérant dans la zone. A travers sa présence, l'APN réaffirme l'engagement du Cameroun en faveur d'une coopération maritime régionale renforcée et d'un dispositif efficace de contrôle. Une participation qui permet également de contribuer aux réflexions communes et de suivre l'évolution des standards régionaux pour un espace maritime africain plus sûr et conforme aux normes internationales. Cet article Mémorandum d’Abuja : l’Autorité portuaire nationale engagée à Libreville pour la sécurité maritime est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Investissement public : 10 communes modèles récompensées par le Minepat
data.description: © DR Le ministre de l'Économie, Alamine Ousmane Mey, a présidé le 22 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé la 2ème édition des Awards des Communes Modèles dans la réalisation des projets d'investissement public. Dix communes, une par région, distinguées pour leur performance au titre de l'exercice 2025 avec une dotation globale de 500 millions de FCFA. La performance locale à l'honneur. Le Ministre de l'Économie, de la Planification et de l'Aménagement du Territoire, Alamine Ousmane Mey, a présidé le 22 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, la deuxième édition des « Awards des Communes Modèles dans la réalisation des Projets d'Investissement Public » au titre de l'exercice 2025. Dix communes lauréates, représentant chacune l'une des dix régions du Cameroun, ont été distinguées. Il s'agit de Ngaoundéré III (Adamaoua), Kobdombo (Centre), Nguelebok (Est), Petté (Extrême-Nord), Loum (Littoral), Touroua (Nord), Nkambe (Nord-Ouest), Pété-Bandjoun (Ouest), Zoétélé (Sud) et Idabato (Sud-Ouest). Chaque commune a reçu une dotation de cinquante millions (50 000 000) de FCFA, soit une enveloppe globale de cinq cents millions (500 000 000) de FCFA. Cette distinction vise à valoriser les bonnes performances des Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées, à encourager l'émulation dans l'exécution des projets d'investissements publics et à renforcer leur impact sur les conditions de vie des populations. A travers cette initiative, le MINEPAT entend promouvoir les bonnes pratiques et la culture de la performance dans la gestion de l'investissement public local, pilier essentiel de la décentralisation. Cet article Investissement public : 10 communes modèles récompensées par le Minepat est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Stratégie sanitaire « America First » : le Cameroun parmi les 7 partenaires africains à New York
data.description: © DR Le Cameroun a participé le 21 septembre 2026 à New York à un dîner de haut niveau marquant le premier anniversaire de la Stratégie mondiale de santé « America First ». Aux côtés de six autres pays africains, Yaoundé a réaffirmé son engagement dans un partenariat de 850 millions de dollars avec Washington, désormais consolidé par la signature du SOAG. Le Cameroun consolide son partenariat sanitaire avec Washington. Le 21 septembre 2026 à New York, le Cameroun a pris part à un dîner de travail de haut niveau organisé à l'occasion du premier anniversaire de la Stratégie mondiale de santé « America First ». Une rencontre qui a réuni 12 parties : des responsables américains initiateurs de la stratégie, le Cameroun et six autres pays africains partenaires que sont la Tanzanie, l'Ouganda, le Nigeria, le Kenya, le Mozambique et l'Éthiopie. Pour Yaoundé, cette stratégie est une opportunité de renforcer visibilité, redevabilité et appropriation nationale. Le partenariat mobilise environ 850 millions de dollars, dont 400 millions apportés par les États-Unis et 450 millions au titre du co-investissement camerounais. Depuis la signature du mémorandum d'entente en décembre 2025, la mise en œuvre s'est accélérée. Le plan de mise en œuvre a été validé en juillet 2026, les indicateurs de performance examinés conjointement, et le 19 septembre 2026, les deux parties ont signé l'Accord d'objectif stratégique (SOAG), qui consolide le cadre opérationnel et financier. Le Cameroun met en place une Unité de gestion du programme et de la transition chargée d'accompagner le renforcement des capacités et la pérennisation des acquis au-delà de 2030. « Chaque dollar investi doit non seulement sauver des vies aujourd'hui, mais aussi contribuer à bâtir des institutions durables », a souligné la partie camerounaise. Cet article Stratégie sanitaire « America First » : le Cameroun parmi les 7 partenaires africains à New York est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Journée Mondiale du Tourisme 2026 : le Mintoul mise sur les médias et l’IA pour repenser le tourisme
data.description: © DR En prélude à la Journée mondiale du tourisme célébrée chaque 27 septembre, le ministère du Tourisme et des Loisirs a lancé le 22 septembre 2026 ses activités par une concertation avec journalistes, influenceurs et créateurs de contenu. Placée sous le thème « Agenda numérique et intelligence artificielle pour repenser le tourisme », l'édition 2026 veut faire du Cameroun une destination innovante et connectée. Le ministère du Tourisme et des Loisirs (MINTOUL) donne le ton. En prélude à la célébration de la Journée Mondiale du Tourisme prévue le 27 septembre 2026, le département ministériel a officiellement lancé ses activités ce lundi 22 septembre par une réunion stratégique rassemblant journalistes, influenceurs, blogueurs et créateurs de contenu numérique. Présidée par le secrétaire général, M. Ndioro A Mamoum, la rencontre visait à renforcer la visibilité médiatique et numérique des festivités du 27 septembre. Le thème retenu cette année, « Agenda numérique et intelligence artificielle pour repenser le tourisme », place la technologie au cœur de la transformation du secteur. Le Secrétaire Général a invité les professionnels des médias et du digital à mettre leurs plateformes au service de la promotion du riche potentiel touristique du Cameroun, tout en soulignant le rôle clé de l'intelligence artificielle dans la modernisation de l'offre, la personnalisation de l'expérience visiteur et la compétitivité de la destination. Cette concertation marque le coup d'envoi d'une semaine d'activités jusqu'au 27 septembre, qui ambitionne de positionner le Cameroun comme une destination touristique dynamique, innovante et résolument tournée vers le numérique. Cet article Journée Mondiale du Tourisme 2026 : le Mintoul mise sur les médias et l’IA pour repenser le tourisme est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le gouvernement prévoit une campagne contre la rougeole-rubéole du 14 au 18 octobre 2026
data.description: © Gavi La grande campagne nationale de suivi contre la rougeole-rubéole, prévue du 16 au 20 septembre 2026, n'a pas eu lieu à la rentrée. Elle est décalée au 14-18 octobre 2026 sur tout le territoire pour répondre à une épidémie ayant déjà fait au moins 18 morts. Le report de la campagne est officiel. L'annonce des ministres de la Santé publique Manaouda Malachie et de l’Éducation de base Laurent Serge Etoundi Ngoa est contenue dans un communiqué conjoint. En cause, des contraintes opérationnelles et une épidémie qui explose avec 9 568 cas et 18 décès dans 120 districts de santé. Comme raisons justifiant le report, les deux ministres parlent de "contraintes opérationnelles". Dans le jargon de la santé publique, cela peut signifier qu’il y a un besoin en logistique massive. Il faut prépositionner des millions de doses de vaccin Rougeole-Rubéole avec chaîne de froid garantie dans 120 districts en épidémie active. Les stocks sont confirmés disponibles, mais leur déploiement sécurisé prend du temps. Cela renvoie aussi à la qualité de la riposte. Les premières mesures de riposte depuis janvier ont permis "une amélioration progressive dans plusieurs zones". Pour transformer cet essai en coup d'arrêt définitif, le gouvernement veut une campagne à 100% de couverture, pas une campagne précipitée. Dans le registre des raisons, le report invite à ne pas saboter la rentrée. Organiser une campagne nationale et une rentrée scolaire les mêmes jours (16-20 sept) aurait surchargé les centres de santé et créé une confusion totale pour les parents. Le report permet de dissocier les deux opérations. Décidé par les membres du gouvernement ce glissement n'est donc pas un abandon, c'est un choix stratégique pour frapper plus fort en octobre. La mesure ne doit pas faire oublier la gravité de la situation. Depuis plus de huit mois, l’épidémie est en cours au pays. Plus de la moitié des districts de santé est touchée. La rougeole est l'une des maladies les plus contagieuses au monde. Un seul enfant malade peut en contaminer 18. Elle tue par ses complications : pneumonies, encéphalites, cécité. Et la rentrée scolaire, avec des milliers d'enfants entassés en classe, est le premier accélérateur de propagation. La situation nécessite ainsi une réponse nationale. Pour cette opération, les ministres imposent un protocole. Pour les parents et tuteurs, avant tout enrôlement, vérifier la complétude du calendrier vaccinal. La 2e dose du vaccin Rougeole-Rubéole, est administrée à partir de 15 mois. Sans elle, l'enfant n'est pas protégé et est contagieux. Pour les écoles maternelles, les directrices doivent vérifier le carnet de tout enfant s'inscrivant pour la première fois. Elles ont eu l’instruction de refuser les premières inscriptions sans preuve de vaccination. Les écoles quant à elles doivent vérifier le statut vaccinal de tous les enfants et orienter les cas présentant une situation vaccinale partielle vers la formation sanitaire la plus proche pour rattrapage. Pour lever toute hésitation, les ministres rassurent des stocks de vaccin rougeole-rubéole en quantité suffisante dans toutes les formations sanitaires. La prise en charge se fait à 100% par le gouvernement via le Programme élargi de vaccination (PEV). Ainsi, "contre la rougeole, vaccinons nos enfants et protégeons-les !" C’est du 14 au 18 octobre prochains dans les 10 régions. Cet article Cameroun : le gouvernement prévoit une campagne contre la rougeole-rubéole du 14 au 18 octobre 2026 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
